tagline: A public registry of Armenian fortresses with a map, sources, and community contributions

about.title: A living map of Armenian fortresses
about.intro: Hayastani Berdry brings fortresses, defensive sites, and historical places into one shared registry: from well-known monuments to locations mostly remembered by local communities.
about.sideNote: We preserve coordinates, historical context, photos, routes, and sources so Armenian heritage can be explored with more care and clarity.
about.cardMapText: Each point is tied to its landscape, making location, nearby settlements, and access conditions easier to understand.
about.cardSourcesText: Entries are backed by links, descriptions, and confidence notes instead of being just a gallery of attractive photos.
about.cardCommunityText: Users can suggest new places and corrections, while admins review the data before it becomes public.

rules.title: How we review and publish materials
rules.intro: The project brings together historical data, local testimony, and field observations. To keep the map useful, every contribution is reviewed and clearly labeled.
rules.evidenceText: Every fortress has a status: verified, partially verified, oral testimony, or needs research.
rules.sourcesText: Historical claims should be linked, when possible, to publications, archives, maps, photos, or other verifiable materials.
rules.testimonyText: Stories from local residents are valuable and allowed, but they must be labeled explicitly as oral testimony.
rules.coordinatesText: Coordinates must include an accuracy label: exact, approximate, or unverified.
rules.reviewText: User submissions are not published immediately. An admin reviews the data and clarifies details when needed.
rules.photosText: Photos must include author, rights holder, or source metadata so materials can be used responsibly.
rules.safetyText: The site does not guarantee safe access to remote, difficult, or border-area locations. Check the current situation and follow local restrictions before traveling.
